headline: US envoy Tom Barrack
dek: Barrack said the US supports Saudi Arabia and will supply needed logistics but is not prepared to send troops: 'America getting involved in a ground kinetic battle somewhere else seems fruitless' / ground intervention 'appears pointless'. Urged Middle East countries to build regional alliances…
sources: Tom Barrack, US envoy to Syria and Iraq (also US ambassador to Türkiye), speaking at the Global Security Forum in Doha
fault_line: America says 'handle it yourselves' while its ally's airport is closed — is this burden-sharing or abandonment?

sections.what_happened: Barrack said the US supports Saudi Arabia and will supply needed logistics but is not prepared to send troops: 'America getting involved in a ground kinetic battle somewhere else seems fruitless' / ground intervention 'appears pointless'. Urged Middle East countries to build regional alliances instead of relying on Washington; US redefining its role away from direct intervention.
sections.what_verified: Dawn (direct link); consistent with ET relay of the same Doha remarks. Directionally consistent with US disengagement posture (Trump's Iran-war focus, sanctions waiver).
sections.what_disputed: Full forum transcript not seen in-window; quotes are relayed by Dawn/ET — seek transcript before using exact wording in narration.
sections.why_matters: The sharpest public articulation of the US disengagement doctrine, delivered in Doha while Saudi Arabia takes hits: Washington offers logistics, not soldiers. Pair with the UK Typhoon announcement — the split screen is the story. TOTW stance: present Barrack's words verbatim-as-reported; the abandonment question is the fault line.
sections.context: Background: US envoy Tom Barrack: ground intervention in Yemen 'appears pointless'; urges regional alliances over US reliance

totw_analysis: Our read: The sharpest public articulation of the US disengagement doctrine, delivered in Doha while Saudi Arabia takes hits: Washington offers logistics, not soldiers. Pair with the UK Typhoon announcement — the split screen is the story. TOTW stance: present Barrack's words verbatim-as-reported; the abandonment question is the fault line.
